title: tool-calling-exec-ergonomics: multi-tool & parallel executions, result injection, retries, and OpenAI-compat streaming fixes
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Added ergonomics for multi-tool and parallel tool calling, tool result injection API, stronger retry semantics, and OpenAI-compat streaming fixes for function/tool calls. Backwards-compatible by default; opt-in gate for strict ordering behavior.
description: Motivation: Customers build tool-enabled agents that need to call multiple tools per turn, sometimes in parallel (e.g., web lookup + calculator). Current tool-calling surface assumed single sequential calls and lacked first-class ergonomics for parallelism, result injection, and transparent retries. This PR introduces API and runtime ergonomics to make multi-tool and parallel tool calls reliable and easy to consume, and fixes streaming behavior in the OpenAI-compat layer so function call markers and tool outputs are emitted consistently during streaming.
commits: 3 commits: 1) api: add MultiToolInvocation envelope and parallel flag + docs; 2) runtime: implement parallel dispatch, tool result injection points, and retry policy hooks; 3) openai-compat: stabilize streaming events for function/tool outputs and add compatibility tests. Each commit is focused and small; the runtime commit contains the majority of implementation and tests.

review_comments: Diego Ramos: Can we ensure default behavior is fully backwards compatible for existing single-function callers? I don't want silent behavior changes in hosted API.
Ava Chen (reply): Default API surface retains single-tool semantics unless MultiToolInvocation is used. Added explicit gauge in docs and tests to assert backwards compatibility.

Priya Patel: The retry policy looks good but we need to surface idempotency keys for tools that are not idempotent (external webhooks). Please add guidance and optional idempotency_id on the invocation envelope.
Ava Chen (reply): Added optional idempotency_id string to the envelope and validated it's passed through to runtime. Docs updated with guidance on idempotent vs non-idempotent tools.

Owen Brooks: Streaming ordering fix in openai_compat looks sane. Confirmed tests exercise the case where a tool begins streaming, another completes, and the model returns a function call marker mid-stream.
Diego Ramos (approve): Approving; tested locally with python sdk example that does parallel web+calc calls and observed stable streaming outputs.
Priya Patel (approve): Approving after idempotency note added.
discussion_thread: Thread: handling partial failures when one of parallel tools fails - we added per-tool result envelopes that include status and error metadata so the caller can decide to retry or fallback.
Thread: retry semantics - runtime supports per-tool retry policy with exponential backoff and a global per-invocation budget to avoid unbounded retries.

Thread: tool result injection - added a deterministic injection point: after all parallel tool outputs are available (or failed/timeout), runtime will synthesize a ToolInvocationResultEnvelope that can be merged back into the model input or streamed as intermediate events depending on the caller's mode.
testing_notes: Unit tests added for serialization/deserialization of the MultiToolInvocation envelope, idempotency key handling, and runtime parallel executor. Integration tests simulate flaky external tools and validate retry/abort behavior and final merged result envelope. OpenAI-compat streaming unit tests verify function_call start/args/end markers are emitted in the correct order even during interleaved tool streams.
compatibility_notes: OpenAI-compat layer preserves existing streaming format for single function calls. New MultiToolInvocation API is opt-in. When callers use openai-compat with multi-tool invocations, the handler will emit function_call markers for each tool invocation and will stream tool outputs as discrete events; consumers should tolerate interleaved tool streaming events. Backwards-compatible by default; feature flagged in experimental_tool_calling toggle for hosted customers.
docs_changes_summary: docs/api/tool-calling.md updated with: 1) API samples (python/ts) showing parallel_invocation usage, 2) best practices for idempotency keys, 3) example of tool result injection into a follow-up model turn, 4) migration notes for existing single-tool users.
